title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of a short passage that begins on the previous page (201). It is a methodological remark, not a computation.

Setting from the surrounding pages. Grothendieck has been parametrising certain automorphisms u in two ways:
- by data (mu, c, d, t, n);
- by triples (alpha, beta, f), with alpha, beta congruent to (1,1) mod 2 and f in a profinite fundamental group.

The triples are subject to the 'relation des lacets'. This loop relation is his name for the relations an automorphism of the profinite pi_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} (or of a related orbifold) must satisfy relative to the standard loops and the rotation of order 3. The aim is to recover the associated element u_{alpha,beta,f} of GL(2, Z-hat)' from such data.

On page 201 the description is clumsy: a Z-hat-torsor of pairs (alpha, beta), a quotient by a diagonal Z-hat action, and a contracted product of the opposite torsor with SL(2, Z-hat), giving an SL(2, Z-hat)-torsor. He comments 'Décidément, ces formulations ne sont pas enthousiasmantes' (these formulations are not inspiring).

This page draws the conclusion. He will have to
1. introduce explicitly, and study at least minimally, 'le groupe adélique', i.e. the group of all systems (alpha, beta, f) satisfying the loop relation (a profinite group mixing Z-hat* and Z-hat-scalars with elements f of the completed free group);
2. write down the canonical homomorphism from M_{0,3}^{!~} into that group. The symbol is uncertain; it is probably a profinite or arithmetic fundamental group attached to M_{0,3}, presumably through which Gal(Q-bar/Q) acts.

He postpones this to first finish the 'gammes rotationnelles' (rotational exercises). Indeed the next page (402) begins section IV, 'Les trois cas particuliers fondamentaux': the case h=1, i.e. [u, sigma_infinity]=1, where he parametrises solutions by couples (xi, f) with xi rho(f) rho^2(f) = 1.

Modern reading. The intended object is a group of pairs or triples (lambda- or alpha-type scalars in Z-hat, f in the completed free group F_2-hat) cut out by loop relations of 2-, 3- and 5-cycle type. It receives a canonical map from an arithmetic fundamental group. This is essentially the conceptual skeleton of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT-hat and the map Gal(Q-bar/Q) -> GT-hat. Here the version involves only the 'rotational' relations around M_{0,3} / genus-1 data (GL_2(Z-hat), SL_2(Z-hat)).
errors: No mathematical claims are made on this page, so there is nothing to check. The program is only announced; the group is neither defined nor shown to be a group here.

Neither this page nor the neighbouring ones establish that the systems (alpha, beta, f) satisfying the loop relation are closed under the composition law. That is the first thing such a definition would require.

ideas.what: Introduce explicitly the profinite ('adelic') group of all systems (alpha, beta, f) satisfying the loop relation, instead of working with torsors under Z-hat and SL(2, Z-hat).
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group (profinite GT-hat, or a 'rotational' variant of it), defined by parameters in Z-hat* × F_2-hat with loop relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: V. Drinfeld (1990); Y. Ihara (1990-91); later Lochak–Schneps, Harbater–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Only the general program appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984): the Teichmüller tower, and Gal(Q-bar/Q) as the automorphism group of the tower. As far as I know, no explicit group of (alpha, beta, f) systems is published by Grothendieck.

ideas.what: Canonical homomorphism from M_{0,3}^{!~} (an arithmetic or profinite fundamental group attached to M_{0,3}) into this group.
ideas.modern_name: Galois representation Gal(Q-bar/Q) -> GT-hat, via the outer action on pi_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi/Grothendieck (injectivity on the outer action); Drinfeld, Ihara (factorisation through GT-hat)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the outer action of Gal on pi_1 of M_{0,3} and M_{0,4} and the Teichmüller tower, but not this explicit map.

ideas.what: Methodological choice: replace torsor and contracted-product formulations by an explicit group.
ideas.modern_name: Passage from torsors to the structure group

missed.claim: In these Longue Marche continuation notes (c. 1981), Grothendieck explicitly plans to define and study the profinite group of all triples (alpha, beta, f) satisfying the 'relation des lacets', together with the canonical homomorphism into it. Conceptually this anticipates the definition of GT-hat (Drinfeld 1990) and the map Gal -> GT-hat (Ihara). On this page it is only announced and postponed.
missed.quote: étudier un minimum de suite le groupe adélique formé par les systèmes (α, β, f) satisfaisant à la relation des lacets, et l'homomorphisme canonique de M_{0,3}^{!~} dans ledit groupe
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents that Grothendieck was heading toward an explicit GT-type group about a decade before Drinfeld. Whether later pages of 140-3 actually define it, and with which relations (here a 'rotational' variant tied to GL_2(Z-hat)' and SL_2(Z-hat)), would be of historical, and possibly mathematical, interest for comparison with GT-hat and its variants.

deep.surprise_reason: The page only announces an intention. Still, the intention is to define explicitly a GT-like 'adelic group' of loop-relation solutions plus a canonical homomorphism into it, written years before Drinfeld and Ihara. Specialists (Schneps, Lochak) know Grothendieck worked in this direction, so it is notable as a historical detail but not a result.
transcription_corrections: The first word is the end of 'explicit-/ement' carried over from the previous page: '-ement et étudier', not 'vient et étudier'.
The last word reads 'gammes rotationnelles' (musical 'exercises'), not 'jougs rotationnels'; the feminine plural 'rotationnelles' is visible in the image.
'[-envoyer-]' is a struck-through word, possibly 'envoyer' or similar, before 'l'homomorphisme canonique'.
The symbol is M_{0,3} with superscripts '!' and '~'; the exact reading is uncertain.
